sources: Union Minister for Ports, Shipping and Waterways Sarbananda Sonowal, X post Nov 11, via Economic Times / Telegraph India / ABP (IANS) / Gulf News liveblog
fault_line: Iran calls the southern route 'unauthorised' and mined; shippers call it international water -- does any tanker sailing without Tehran's permission become a legitimate target?

sections.what_happened: [VERIFIED FACT -- the strike and the casualties] A projectile struck the Liberia-flagged VLCC MT FUJAIRAH ENERGY while transiting the Persian/Arabian Gulf from Al Ruwais to on Tuesday Nov 10. Four crew members were injured, including one Indian national (minor injuries, taken ashore for further medical examination). 24 crew aboard incl. 6 Indian seafarers; the remaining 18 crew (incl. the other 5 Indians) are safe and accounted for. [ATTRIBUTION UNKNOWN] No claimant and no attribution to any actor in any tiered source: do NOT attribute to Iran, the IRGC or the Ansar Allah. [SEPARATE INCIDENT -- DO NOT MERGE] This is NOT the UKMTO Warning 201-26 projectile strike northeast of Oman's Lima village (already covered) and NOT any of the mine incidents in the Strait of Hormuz (1400-02): different location (Arabian Gulf, Al Ruwais- route), different weapon (projectile, not mine), named vessel with named casualty figures. [PORTWATCH BACKBONE] IMF PortWatch snapshot 2026-11-11 (fetched 10:03 , NOT stale, lag 3 days): counted 3 total transits through Hormuz on 2026-11-08 (1 tanker); 7-day average 3.86 vs a calendar-2025 baseline of 85.53/day (4.5% of baseline). Cite only as a counted figure with its observation date, never as live traffic.
sections.what_verified: 2 distinct families: the primary source itself (Indian Ministry of Ports, Shipping and Waterways, Sonowal X post -- T1 official/primary) + Gulf News (T3, own liveblog item 07:39 ). Economic Times, Telegraph India, ABP (IANS), India TV, The Statesman, CNBC-TV18 and Deccan Herald all carry the same minister post but have NO declared tier in the registry and do not count toward corroboration.
sections.what_disputed: No independent (non-minister) confirmation of the projectile's origin, the damage extent, or the vessel's current status has been published. UKMTO has issued no advisory naming Fujairah Energy. The vessel's flag (Liberia), route and crew figures come solely from the minister's post as carried.
sections.why_matters: A named tanker, four injured crew, one minister on the record -- the Gulf shipping war just put a name and a number on its newest victim.
sections.context: Background: MISSED CATCH-UP (event Tue Nov 10; first publication Nov 11 ~09:40-10:13 via Indian minister's X post; missed by the 10:00, 11:00, 12:00 and 13:00 scans) -- Projectile strikes Liberia-flagged VLCC MT Fujairah Energy in the Arabian Gulf; 4 crew injured

totw_analysis: Our read: A named tanker, four injured crew, one minister on the record -- the Gulf shipping war just put a name and a number on its newest victim. The fault line our audience is arguing over: Iran calls the southern route 'unauthorised' and mined; shippers call it international water -- does any tanker sailing without Tehran's permission become a legitimate target?
